places.name: Streets and squares of the centre
places.baseNote: Section 59 UrhG lets you photograph and publish works permanently on public paths, roads and open spaces. For buildings that covers the façade.

drone: Section 21h(3) LuftVO puts government seats, embassies, police property, federal trunk roads, railway installations and federal waterways off limits without consent. The centre is covered several times over.

places.name: Humboldt Forum, outdoor areas
places.baseNote: The foundation's guidelines allow photography here for commercial and non-commercial purposes, and explicitly allow tripods and flash.

drone: Aerial shots in the outdoor areas need prior permission from the foundation, applied for at least 14 days ahead, and the airspace restrictions still apply on top.

places.name: Humboldt Forum, foyer and roof terrace
places.baseNote: Private, non-commercial photography is permitted. This is where the Unter den Linden view is taken from.

tripod: Tripods are not permitted indoors at the Humboldt Forum.
flash: Objects in the display areas are light-sensitive and may only be photographed without flash.
drone: Indoors, and inside a restricted airspace zone.

places.name: Humboldt Forum, 2nd and 3rd floors
places.where: Ethnologisches Museum, Museum für Asiatische Kunst
places.baseNote: Visitors may photograph for their own private use. Any commercial use needs prior permission.

tripod: Tripods are not permitted indoors at the Humboldt Forum.
flash: No flash on the display objects.
camera: Fine to carry, but the state museums' rules count a camera case as a bulky object to be checked in.

places.name: Humboldt Forum, BERLIN GLOBAL
places.baseNote: All photographic and film recordings are strictly prohibited, private and commercial alike, because of third-party rights. Pictograms mark the motifs.

places.name: Humboldt Forum, Humboldt Lab
places.baseNote: All photography and filming is prohibited, whether private or commercial. Only prior written permission changes that.

places.name: Neues Museum
places.baseNote: Private photography is normal. The museum regulations do not ban it, but the management board may ban it in any single exhibition or room.

tripod: Tripods are named as bulky objects that must be checked into the cloakroom or a locker.
selfie: Selfie sticks are prohibited in the exhibition rooms.
camera: The camera is fine. Its case is named as a bulky object and goes to the cloakroom.
daypack: Bags and backpacks larger than 30 x 20 x 10 cm must be checked in.
suitcase: Storage is very limited and the museums cannot accommodate anything bigger than carry-on luggage.

places.name: Altes Museum
places.baseNote: Same shared museum regulations as the rest of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.

tripod: Tripods must be checked into the cloakroom or a locker.
camera: Camera cases count as bulky objects and are checked in.
daypack: Anything larger than 30 x 20 x 10 cm goes to the cloakroom.
suitcase: Nothing bigger than carry-on luggage can be stored.

places.name: Alte Nationalgalerie
places.baseNote: Painting galleries are the rooms where a temporary show is most likely to carry its own photography ban, so read the sign at that door.

tripod: Tripods must be checked into the cloakroom or a locker.
daypack: Anything larger than 30 x 20 x 10 cm goes to the cloakroom.
suitcase: Nothing bigger than carry-on luggage can be stored.

places.name: Bode-Museum
places.baseNote: The quietest of the five houses, and the easiest place on the island to photograph without a crowd in the frame.

tripod: Tripods must be checked into the cloakroom or a locker.
daypack: Anything larger than 30 x 20 x 10 cm goes to the cloakroom.
suitcase: Nothing bigger than carry-on luggage can be stored.

places.name: Pergamonmuseum. Das Panorama
places.where: Am Kupfergraben, beside the closed Pergamonmuseum
places.baseNote: The rotunda runs under the same museum regulations. It is the one part of the Pergamon complex you can still walk into.

tripod: Tripods must be checked into the cloakroom or a locker.
daypack: Anything larger than 30 x 20 x 10 cm goes to the cloakroom.
suitcase: Nothing bigger than carry-on luggage can be stored.

places.name: Berlin TV Tower
places.baseNote: Private photos are permitted at the top. Security is airport-style and every bag is opened.

tripod: The tower states plainly that tripods are not permitted.
drone: The tower states plainly that drones are not permitted.
daypack: A backpack has to fit inside 45 x 35 x 20 cm, and there are no lockers at all.
suitcase: Suitcases, large bags and shopping bags may not go up, and the tower has no lockers.

places.name: Memorial, Field of Stelae
places.baseNote: Open ground, free, and covered by the same panorama rule as the streets. Legal is not the whole question here.

drone: Inside the government-quarter restriction zone and beside federal roads.

places.name: Memorial, Information Centre
places.baseNote: Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 18:00, last admission 45 minutes before closing, closed Mondays. The foundation asks for appropriate behaviour in the exhibition.

suitcase: Suitcases and small bags may not be taken into the exhibition. Lockers are at Friedrichstraße and Potsdamer Platz stations.
daypack: Entry is through a security gate, and bags are the reason the queue moves slowly.
